Three recovery patterns, with different tradeoffs

1Checkpoint + restart

Stop the training job, restore durable state, resume.

2Continue with healthy replicas

TorchFT reduces membership so healthy replicas keep training.

3Recover and rejoin the failed replica

Monarch orchestrates recovery; TorchFT restores current state and rejoins it.

TorchFT: keep training while one replica group recovers

Where training goodput goes during a failure

At scale, recovery becomes an efficiency problem

Failure becomes the norm, not the exception: it happens far more often.

4 devices
128 devices
1,024 devices
Failure frequencyhow often failures happen× Blast radiushealthy capacity each one affects× Recovery durationhow long recovery takes

= healthy accelerator time not doing useful work

SERVINGMinimize time below full serving capacity
TRAININGMinimize healthy accelerator time that is not creating new progress

At large scale, failures are expected. The architecture determines how much healthy capacity each failure affects, and for how long.

What we covered today

SERVINGOne failed replica costs capacity, not availability.

Observer and Device Taints detect and isolate the fault fast. Most of the recovery time goes to getting the replacement ready, so pay that cost before the failure.

TRAININGOne failed rank stalls the whole job.

Goodput goes to rollback and replay, stall, and recovery overhead. TorchFT and Monarch keep the healthy replicas training while the failed one recovers and rejoins.

Recap: Keep useful work moving through failure

1PROVE HEALTH
Observer Health Check

Actively validate accelerator health before placing expensive work.

2CONTAIN FAILURE
Observer passive monitoring + DRA Device Taints

Detect faults quickly and keep unhealthy capacity from affecting more work.

3PRESERVE PROGRESS
TorchFT + Monarch orchestration

Keep healthy training replicas progressing while the failed replica recovers and rejoins.

SERVINGStay available and restore full serving capacity quickly.
TRAININGPreserve useful progress and maximize goodput.

Failures are inevitable. Lost useful work does not have to be.
